200.title: Krakow attacker may be influenced by 'far-right ideologies': Polish interior minister
200.summary: Initial indications suggest that the suspect who opened fire in central Krakow, Poland's second-largest city, was influenced by far-right ideologies, Interior Minister Marcin Kierwinski said late Saturday. Preliminary findings suggest the attacker was influenced by far-right ideologies and held ultranationalist views, although those indications have yet to be verified, according to Kierwinski.
200.body: Initial indications suggest that the suspect who opened fire in central Krakow, Poland's second-largest city, was influenced by far-right ideologies, Interior Minister Marcin Kierwinski said late Saturday. He confirmed that six people were killed, including one foreign national, while 16 were injured, including five foreign nationals, two police officers and the suspect. Preliminary findings suggest the attacker was influenced by far-right ideologies and held ultranationalist views, although those indications have yet to be verified, according to Kierwinski. They appeared to be close family members of the attacker, he added. 'Until now in Poland we haven't had such drastic cases of terrorism ... that's what we have to call this cruel attack on people's lives here in Krakow,' said Tusk.

400.title: Europe Faces Energy Crisis as Gas Reserves Hit Lowest Level Since 2011
400.summary: Europe is entering winter with alarmingly low gas reserves, the lowest level recorded since 2011, which raises significant concerns for households facing potential spikes in energy costs. Rising energy prices are becoming a pressing supply chain issue, but Brussels has asserted that energy supplies are not in immediate jeopardy.
400.body: Europe is entering winter with alarmingly low gas reserves, the lowest level recorded since 2011, which raises significant concerns for households facing potential spikes in energy costs. Rising energy prices are becoming a pressing supply chain issue, but Brussels has asserted that energy supplies are not in immediate jeopardy. However, disagreements persist over energy taxes and the concept of joint energy purchases among member nations. Across Europe, the tight gas supplies have significant implications for household bills and energy policies.

400.title: How cloudy weather is causing a problem for Europe’s solar boom
400.summary: Europe risks entering its first ‘dunkelflaute’ of the year as cloudy weather dampens the continent’s solar boom and sends energy prices soaring.
400.body: Europe risks entering its first ‘dunkelflaute’ of the year as cloudy weather dampens the continent’s solar boom and sends energy prices soaring. According to Bloomberg forecasts, German day-ahead power prices for Thursday 29 October were above €300 a megawatt-hour, about double the average in October, with hourly rates hitting above €500 for the evening peak.‘It’s extremely disheartening’: Home solar output dipsOn an individual scale, households with solar panels are also noticing a spike in their energy bills. One UK resident who has 12 solar panels installed on their roof with a combined capacity of 6.36 kW tells Euronews Earth that on Wednesday (4 November) the panels only produced 10.90 kWh of solar – leaving them to rely on the grid for an additional 27.40 kWh of energy required.

500.body: Built in Copilot Studio, the agent allows employees to ask questions about HR policies and benefits instead of manually contacting an HR representative. Within 30 days, the agent became the second most-used agent at State Farm, out of more than 3,000 AI agent identities within the Power Platform environment. From answering questions to getting work done for customers State Farm’s next chapter builds on what teams have already proven with knowledge-based agents. 500.title: DeepSeek Nears OpenAI’s Cyber Model in Vals Test at $3 a Run
500.summary: An open-weight DeepSeek model came close to OpenAI’s restricted cyber model on a new benchmark from evaluation firm Vals AI, at about a tenth of the cost per run, according to Vals’ CyberOffense leaderboard.
500.body: An open-weight DeepSeek model came close to OpenAI’s restricted cyber model on a new benchmark from evaluation firm Vals AI, at about a tenth of the cost per run, according to Vals’ CyberOffense leaderboard. The key insight: Vals AI's CyberOffense leaderboard puts OpenAI's restricted GPT-6 Sol Daybreak first and the open-weight DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 close behind, at under $3 per run against about $22, per Vals. Vals AI, CyberOffense leaderboard “The gap that used to separate a restricted frontier model from a freely available one is now small.” Three Implications FOR OPENAI Vals lists GPT-6 Sol Daybreak first, a model it says OpenAI offers only through its restricted Daybreak cyber program. Read the Map of AI → The Bottom Line On Vals AI’s CyberOffense test, OpenAI’s restricted GPT-6 Sol Daybreak led, and the open-weight DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 came within about 8 points overall by our arithmetic, at under $3 per run against about $22, per Vals.
